$comment: Hand-authored compatibility floors for the release manifest. Every field here MUST name a consumer that acts on it, and that consumer must exist. A declared dependency nothing enforces is decoration, and decoration in a health surface is the exact defect this repo spent 17-18 Aug 2026 removing: a true fact nobody can act on reads as noise and trains people to ignore the surface.

Deliberately absent: contractVersion, which scripts/release-artifacts.mjs derives from packages/tool-contract/package.json. Restating it here would create two sources of truth for one fact, and the drift would be invisible.

Also deliberately absent: any floor on the backend. api.ascenda.one is continuously deployed and is always the newest build, so a minimum backend version is a number that can never be false — which makes it worthless as a check.

$minCollectorVersion.means: Oldest collector release still considered current. Below this, a running installation is out of date.
consumers: apps/macos Connections row — states the version alongside 'last seen', without colour or reproach

packages/tool-kit/src/releaseCheck.ts — the collectors' background sender reads this floor from the latest release manifest once a day, and a hook below it says so at the start of every session until it's updated
$minCollectorVersion.how the collectors read it: Never from the bundle, which always meets its own floor, and never on a hook's path or in status. The detached flusher fetches the latest manifest after it drains; hooks and status only read what it saved. An unpaired install starts no flusher and fetches nothing.
$minCollectorVersion.why 0.1.9: First release whose sends are journalled (~/.ascenda/state). Below it, a failing collector is undiagnosable, which is the floor's whole purpose.

$minMacosAppVersion.means: Oldest Ascenda Flow build for macOS that can render what these collectors emit.
consumers: apps/macos/tools/appcast-requires.mjs — emits it into the Sparkle appcast item as <ascendaRequires>
the app's SPUUpdaterDelegate — reads that element to tell a user their app is behind its tools
$minMacosAppVersion.why 0.1.2: Current shipping build; no collector field yet requires more. Raise this only when a collector emits something an older app renders wrongly — never merely because a newer app exists.
